title: LLaVA: Visual Instruction Tuning
hook: Connect a CLIP vision encoder to an LLM with just a linear projection, fine-tune on GPT-4-generated image dialogues, and get a capable open chat-with-images model for under a day of training.
key_points: A small linear layer bridges a frozen CLIP encoder and a frozen LLM - no heavyweight fusion architecture needed.
Training data was GPT-4-generated conversations about images, sidestepping expensive human annotation.
Instruction tuning on this data gave strong visual question-answering and reasoning despite the simple design.
Fully open weights and recipe sparked a wave of follow-on multimodal models.
content_html: Liu and colleagues at UW-Madison and Microsoft released LLaVA in April 2023, showing that a surprisingly simple architecture could turn a text-only LLM into a capable visual assistant. The key ingredient was instruction-tuning data generated by GPT-4 from image captions and bounding-box descriptions, avoiding the need for human annotators to label image-dialogue pairs at scale.
extra_html:
How it works

A frozen CLIP image encoder extracts visual features, which a single trainable linear projection maps into the same embedding space as the LLM's text tokens. Those projected tokens are prepended to the text prompt and the whole sequence passes through a (mostly frozen) LLM. Instruction tuning on the GPT-4-generated dialogues teaches the model to answer questions, describe scenes, and reason about image content.

Why it matters

LLaVA proved that you don't need a bespoke multimodal architecture to get strong vision-language results - a minimal connector plus good data is enough. The open weights and reproducible recipe made it a foundation for dozens of follow-up models and practical applications. Read the full paper on arXiv.

related.title: CLIP: Learning Visual Models from Language
related.hook: Skip the fixed label list. Train on image–caption pairs so pictures and text share one space, and you can classify images from plain-text labels you make up on the spot.

related.title: Flamingo: a Visual Language Model for Few-Shot Learning
related.hook: Interleave images and text in a prompt, use cross-attention to inject visual features into a frozen LLM, and get few-shot image understanding without retraining the language model.

related.title: GPT-4o: One Model for Text, Audio, and Vision
related.hook: GPT-4o is a single model that natively processes text, audio, and images end-to-end - no separate speech pipeline - cutting voice response latency to near human conversational speed.

related.title: FLAN: Instruction Tuning
related.hook: Teach a model to follow many tasks phrased as plain instructions, and it learns to follow instructions for tasks it never saw — zero-shot.

flashcards.prompt: How does LLaVA connect a CLIP vision encoder to an LLM?
flashcards.back_html: With a single trainable linear projection that maps CLIP's visual features into the LLM's text-token embedding space; the projected tokens are prepended to the prompt.

choices.text: Crowdsourced human annotators labeling image dialogues

flashcards.explanation_html: LLaVA used GPT-4 to generate image dialogues from captions and bounding-box descriptions, sidestepping expensive human annotation.

flashcards.prompt: What was LLaVA's main lesson about multimodal model design?

choices.text: A minimal connector plus good data can rival bespoke fusion architectures
Only end-to-end training of all components yields strong results
Vision-language tasks require far larger models than text-only ones

flashcards.explanation_html: LLaVA showed you don't need a heavyweight multimodal architecture — a simple connector and good instruction data suffice.
